findings: F1-73-hardware: reset reads address 0 "on Armv7-M unless VTOR is changed" -> address 0 on the Cortex-M3; Armv7-M VTOR resets to zero unless the implementation provides configuration inputs (D1 §2.3.4; D13 B3.2.5)
F1-73-jargon: MCU has on-chip non-volatile program memory (usually flash) -> on-chip flash on many parts, or an external QSPI flash chip as on the RP2350 (D10 §1, §4.4)
F1-73-l2-startup: SRAM contents are not defined after power-up (Yiu, not opened) -> the core's reset sequence sets registers and writes nothing to memory (D13 B1.5.5)

F1-73-l3-contract: how QEMU virt reaches 0x80000000 with -bios none: unverified box -> QEMU 8.2.2 resets at 0x1000 (MROM), a ten-word program jumps to the RAM base 0x80000000 (D12 hw/riscv/boot.c, virt.c, cpu_bits.h)
F1-73-l3-contract: RISC-V reset vector and mtvec claims rested on an unopened spec -> confirmed: "The pc is set to an implementation-defined reset vector"; mtvec (D8 §2.1.4, §2.1.1.7)
F1-73-hardware: UART0 base 0x40004000 only from QEMU memory tree (unverified box) -> confirmed by AN385 APB memory map; SYSCLK 25 MHz (D11 §3.7 Table 3-4, §4)
F1-73-l3-freestanding: C++20 forward-progress rule cited to the current draft -> cited to N4861, the C++20 draft the -std=c++20 build follows (D14 [intro.progress])
F1-73-hardware: boot memory chosen by boot pins or option bytes (Yiu) -> replaced by the documented AN385 low-memory remap, which QEMU does not implement (D11 Table 3-1; D6 §mps2)
F1-73-answers: used attribute stops only the compiler (no source) -> confirmed: on ELF, used alone does not stop linker section GC; retain or KEEP does (D15 used, retain)
